html:
The spread of Islam in Bosnia followed the Ottoman conquest of 1463, and by the early 1600s Muslims made up a majority or near majority of the population.

Conversion was mostly voluntary and gradual. Landholding, office and lower taxes drew nobles and townsmen, and the weak Bosnian Church offered little resistance. Some boys were also taken by the devshirme levy into Ottoman service, among them the grand vizier Mehmed Paša Sokolović. Towns such as Sarajevo and Mostar grew around mosques, markets and bridges like the Stari Most. The converts kept their Slavic language. Their descendants, the Bosniaks, are today the largest people of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
sum: The spread of Islam in Bosnia followed the Ottoman conquest of 1463, and by the early 1600s Muslims made up a majority or near majority of the population.
